mcp.validation_hint: synapse-bridge autostarts the shared local sidecar and connects over loopback; confirm ~/.synapse/sidecar.json exists and GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health returns {"ok":true}, or run the host's MCP status command.

local_wiring: VS Code MCP: mcp.json servers.synapse in the VS Code user data root (auto-generated/merged)
notes: First-party MCP built from mcps/synapse; not an external submodule, so it carries no source_url/path/commit pin.
Zero-config: synapse-bridge reads the bearer token from ~/.synapse/token and autostarts the shared sidecar; no secret is ever written into a host config file.
Project isolation is derived from the bridge process working directory (git root); hosts that launch stdio servers in the open workspace get correct per-project memory automatically.
Generated by default only for first-party secretless MCP services; external or secret-bearing MCPs remain opt-in through --category mcps --service <id>.
Install/update the binary and always-on sidecar service with mcps/synapse/install.mjs (npm run install:synapse).

The always-on service is macOS-only (launchd). Linux and Windows rely on the bridge's lazy autostart: the first bridge launch elects itself to spawn the shared sidecar and later launches reuse it, so no service manager is involved and none is installed.

The installer runs under Node on every platform, so native Windows uses the same recipe as POSIX. It writes the launcher in the platform idiom: a `#!/bin/sh` script on POSIX and a `.cmd` shim on Windows, where there is no shebang — hence the second detect path. Both pin the absolute Node the installer version-gated and re-check the floor at launch.

linux.source: apt nodejs (Debian/Ubuntu; distro nodejs may predate the floor — re-detect verifies)

win32.source: winget OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS (unattended; machine-wide install needs elevation)

mcp.validation_hint: Install the pinned openosint application, then call the host MCP status command or an OpenOSINT lookup tool. Tools backed by optional API keys or external binaries report their own missing prerequisite.

local_wiring: MCP-capable runtimes: opt-in cybersecurity MCP named openosint over stdio.
notes: agent-surface provisions openosint via uv (uv tool install openosint==2.27.0) with its provider extras (shodan, censys, openai, ollama); the extras are detected inside openosint's own uv-tool interpreter so an installed launcher never masks a missing provider library.

That interpreter is located by asking the detected uv (`uv tool dir`) rather than assuming a layout: uv's tool directory differs per platform (~/.local/share/uv/tools vs %APPDATA%/uv/data/tools on Windows) and is redirectable, so a hard-coded path would report a successful install as missing extras and drop the service.

Censys is probed as `censys.search`, not `censys`: the distribution installs a PEP 420 namespace package, so a bare `censys` resolves against any directory of that name on sys.path and would read satisfied with the client library absent. The other three ship a regular package and are probed by their top-level name.

Windows bootstraps uv with Astral's standalone PowerShell installer rather than WinGet: it targets %USERPROFILE%/.local/bin, which is a declared detect path, so uv installed at the start of a run is found and used later in that same run. A WinGet portable package lands outside the running process's PATH and would break that bootstrap.

PowerShell 7 (pwsh) is preferred over Windows PowerShell for that install: an install started from a pwsh terminal exports a PSModulePath pointing at PowerShell 7's modules, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 launched under it fails to load its own (Get-ExecutionPolicy is reported as unloadable). -ExecutionPolicy is not passed either, since `iex` of a downloaded string is not governed by it and requesting it pulls in that same module.
Some lookups require external binaries or operator-provided API keys.

All provider keys are OPTIONAL: OpenOSINT runs keyless and each key only enables its provider. Names are taken from the upstream project's documented .env keys; confirm against the pinned release when wiring live credential delivery.
